sources: dossier=Net position bullet 2 + Required behaviors bullet 3 (invariant 4b: producer-advertised ScopesConflict is consulted at acquisition, byte-equal is only the non-advertising fallback) and Corrections-and-restorations 'ScopesConflict had zero callers'; doc(before)=claim-scope.md:11 'Compared byte-equally by the rimsky-side conflict predicate ... no producer-specific code', :38 unconditional byte-equality invariant, :45 pitfall stated as universal; code=runner_acquire_claims.go scopesConflict() delegates to s.ScopesConflict when caps.SupportsScopesConflict, else ClaimScopesByteEqual; test=locks/conflict_test.go covers only the byte-equal fallback.
note: Dossier corroborates via Net position, Required behaviors, and the Corrections record (ScopesConflict wired in as a ruled gap-closure fix); code confirms the delegation. Doc stated byte-equality as the only, unconditional predicate. Rewrote 'What it is', Purpose intro, rationale point 1, the Invariants line, and the pitfall to state byte-equality is the default and describe the producer-delegated scopes-conflict path.

sources: dossier=Corrections-and-restorations 'Doc-stale rationale' entry (transcript, names finding 35, same paragraph as this row) plus Required behaviors bullet 3 (ScopesConflict is the real mechanism for honoring differently-spelled-but-overlapping selectors); doc(before)=claim-scope.md:29 rationale point 2 attributes cross-selector unification purely to open-time canonicalization; code=runner_acquire_claims.go:35/145 candidateScope is json.Marshal(spec.Selector) computed and compared pre-Open, so producer-canonical bytes never reach the candidate side of a byte-equal comparison.
note: Same underlying stale rationale as row 35 (same paragraph, same dossier-named fix). The technical detail about pre-Open timing confirms canonicalization-at-open cannot by itself unify differently-spelled selectors; scopes-conflict is the actual mechanism. Resolved by the same rationale-point-2 rewrite applied for row 35.

sources: dossier=Corrections-and-restorations, 'Doc-stale rationale (2026-07-13, 3f71f90a, transcript): the claim-scope concept doc's byte-equality-only canonicalization rationale predates SupportsScopesConflict; adjudicated fix-doc (finding 35) — rewrite the rationale; code and the claim-producer concept/story already agree.'; doc(before)=claim-scope.md:29 rationale point 2; code=runner_acquire_claims.go:35,43,145 (candidate scope is raw marshaled selector, compared pre-Open).
note: Directly named and adjudicated in the dossier's transcript-tier Corrections section. Rewrote rationale point 2 to describe canonicalization-at-open as one option and scopes-conflict advertisement as the alternative for honoring differently-spelled selectors, matching claim-producer.md's invariant 4b framing.

sources: dossier=silent on the empty-producer-return persistence case; doc=claim-scope.md:30 'The persisted claim scope bytes are exactly what the producer returned. No lossy normalization happens at the rimsky persistence boundary.'; code=runner_acquire_claims.go:35,68 seed ClaimScopeData with rimsky's json.Marshal(spec.Selector) at Insert, and :110 UpdateClaimScope only fires when len(cr.ClaimScope) > 0 and differs — so an empty producer-returned scope leaves rimsky-marshaled selector bytes persisted, not producer-returned bytes; proto claim_producer.proto documents claim_scope 'may be empty' as a supported producer behavior.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): the empty-open fallback is intended — when the producer's open returns no claim scope bytes, the persisted scope remains rimsky's JSON-marshaled resolved selector seeded before open, keeping the scope meaningful for audit and conflict detection. Audit-trail-honesty rationale qualified in claim-scope.md; dossier updated; no code change.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 2 + Required behaviors bullet 3 (scopes-conflict path has no rimsky-side empty guard; that guard is specific to the byte-equal default); doc(before)=claim-scope.md:38 states the empty-never-conflicts rule unconditionally; code=runner_acquire_claims.go:189-196 scopesConflict() passes scope bytes (including empty ones) straight to s.ScopesConflict with no rimsky-side guard when SupportsScopesConflict; locks/conflict.go:24-29 shows the empty guard lives only in ClaimScopesByteEqual (the fallback).
note: Marked duplicate_of 33 by phase 1 — same underlying drift (unconditional byte-equality/empty-never-conflict framing vs. the producer-delegated path). Resolved by the same Invariants-section rewrite applied for row 33, which now scopes the empty-never-conflicts guarantee to the default predicate only.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 2 + Required behaviors bullet 3 + Corrections-and-restorations 'ScopesConflict had zero callers'; doc(before)=claim-scope.md:11 and :38 document only the byte-equal fallback and claim 'no producer-specific code'; code=runner_acquire_claims.go:192-195 s.ScopesConflict(ctx, a, b) invoked when caps.SupportsScopesConflict; neighbor doc=claim-producer.md:17 documents the same capability and calls byte-equal the behavior 'producers that don't advertise' get, i.e. the fallback, not the rule.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors bullet 5 ('Recursive scope partitioning: SplitScope returns sub-scope descriptors; rimsky opens one sub-claim per descriptor', 2026-05-15, data-platform-extensions, artifact); doc(before)=claim-scope.md:11 defined claim scope only as what 'a claim producer's open verb returns'; code=runner_subclaim.go:114,147 persist ClaimScopeData from SplitScopeResponse SubScopeDescriptor.claim_scope_data, not from an Open call; neighbor doc=claim-producer.md:16 documents split-scope as a scope source ('Rimsky opens one sub-claim per sub-scope').
note: Dossier's split-scope required-behavior entry corroborates the code and claim-producer.md's documentation of split-scope as a second scope-origin path. Rewrote the 'What it is' definition to name both the open verb and the split-scope verb as claim scope sources.

sources: dossier=silent on selector substitution timing wording specifically; doc(before)=claim-scope.md:17 parenthetical '(post-substitution)' on the author-supplied selector text contradicts the same sentence's 'may still carry unresolved substitution directives at template-author time, resolved at dispatch', and contradicts the doc's own pitfalls bullet at :44 ('what the template author writes (and may contain unresolved substitution directives)'); code=runner_acquire_claims.go:35 spec.Selector is the dispatch-time-resolved text the producer receives.
note: Self-contradiction within the doc's own body (line 17 vs line 44), independently corroborated by the doc's own pitfalls section describing the pre-substitution author-supplied form. Reworded the selector bullet to state clearly that the author-supplied text may carry unresolved directives and resolves at dispatch, removing the misapplied '(post-substitution)' parenthetical.

sources: dossier=silent on the term pick-policy; doc(before)=claim-scope.md:18 uses 'pick-policy-picked identifier' with no definition anywhere in the concept catalog; code=lib/services/claim_producers/filesystem/store/pick_policy.go implements a producer that picks among available candidates rather than matching a literal selector (functions runPickPolicy/openPickPolicy/popOne); corroborating doc=conformance.md:37 also uses 'pick-policy' unglossed, confirming it is an established but undefined term across the corpus.
note: Undefined noun in the core definition of the concept; corroborated by a second concept doc using the same term the same way, and by the reference implementation's semantics (a producer that picks a candidate rather than matching a selector). Added a short inline gloss ('a producer that picks among candidates rather than matching a literal selector') at first use, self-contained per the design-doc rule.

sources: dossier=silent on substitution-path byte handling for claim_scope; doc=claim-scope.md:20 'A claim-scope substitution path returns the resolved claim scope bytes verbatim into the consuming attribute path.'; code=lib/graph/attribute/substitution.go:317-325,394-399 resolveClaimValue calls stringifyRaw(cr.ClaimScope), which json.Unmarshal-tests the bytes as a JSON string and returns the unquoted string content when they are one, falling back to raw bytes only otherwise; the same stringifyRaw function is used identically for the address substitution path.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): the substitution leaf's JSON-string unquoting is the intentional general stringification convention shared with the address path — substitution splices values into text templates, so quote characters would be serialization artifacts. 'Verbatim' wording replaced in claim-scope.md with the stringification description; dossier updated; no code change.
